clue.text: American money kept in enclosed part of building

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held inside it, so the money sits within the other piece

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in or enclosed
a dime is a ten-cent coin of the US

explanation.surface: Some dollars have been locked away in a closed-off room of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico, an architectural feature of the facade.

clue.text: Right of a racial group to withhold name

indicators.note: withholding something means keeping it back, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: ethnical is an old adjective meaning relating to an ethnic or racial group

explanation.surface: A claim about whether an ethnic community may keep its name secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct is morally right or proper, so the adjective fits 'right' in that moral sense.

clue.text: Archdeacon appearing within elected politician's list

indicators.note: something appearing within another thing turns up inside it, so these letters go into the middle

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is said to be in
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title given to an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A church dignitary turns up on the agenda of a newly elected member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: An Archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven; the possessive on politician's is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a detailed itemised record of goods, a kind of list.

clue.text: Make certain criticism does not involve leading clubs

indicators.note: a thing that does not involve something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: censure is strong disapproval or criticism

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is the one at its front

explanation.surface: Ensure that the critique never drags in the top golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading clubs' gives C, the first letter of clubs, and 'does not involve' removes it from CENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to guarantee that it happens, so it means to make sure.

clue.text: Established authority for existing exponents of mathematics?

definitions.meaning: the people in charge, those holding official power
powers in maths are exponents, and things that 'be' exist, so this is a whimsical reading of the phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: mathematical powers that exist.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the people or bodies holding official control, the authorities.

clue.text: Support for architrave? You can count on it

definitions.meaning: in classical architecture the flat slab on top of a column's capital carries the architrave
a frame of beads on wires used to do arithmetic

explanation.walkthrough: 'You can count on it' looks like an idiom meaning reliability; read literally it describes a counting frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the slab crowning a column's capital and a bead frame for calculating.

clue.text: Served mushroom inside, with general approval

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, splitting it

parts.note: to serve as chairman is to act as one, so served can mean acted
a cep is a large edible mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: A dish with a mushroom in it went down well with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' suggests food being dished up, but here it is serving in a role, as one serves or acts as chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accepted is generally agreed upon or approved by most people.

clue.text: Language machine secretary uses

indicators.note: the run of words uses the answer's letters within it, so the language is concealed across them

explanation.surface: Which tongue does the secretary's typewriter work in?
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese is the language of China, such as Mandarin or Cantonese.

clue.text: Demonstrated better centre for synthetic fabric

parts.note: to sit in is to stage a sit-in protest, so demonstrated can be 'sat in'

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, losing the first and last

explanation.surface: Someone showed the inside of a superior synthetic cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrated' looks like 'showed', but it is the protest sense: SAT IN, as at a sit-in. The centre of 'better' is ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinette is a cheap imitation satin, often woven from cotton or man-made fibres.

clue.text: Herbs one must apply cold to skin rash

indicators.note: applying one thing to another puts it against the front of it here

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hives is an itchy skin rash, also called urticaria

explanation.surface: Advice that a person with an itchy rash should put an ice pack on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are a slender onion-flavoured plant used in cooking, a culinary herb.

clue.text: Set one's cap at random, being unrealistic

indicators.note: letters arranged at random are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, and one's is I'S, here read as I plus S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flirting with someone haphazardly, as the expression to set one's cap at goes, is pure fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'set one's cap at' someone is an old idiom for trying to win them; here it is just anagram fodder, with one's giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapist seeks to avoid real life through fantasy, so the word describes someone not facing reality.

clue.text: Summary of play Racine composed — so gripping

indicators.note: something gripping another holds it inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something composed is put together, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Jean Racine wrote a gripping synopsis of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Racine is the French dramatist, which makes 'play' look like his drama; his name is only the letters for 'composed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a written outline of the plot of a play or film.

clue.text: Homer, possibly, is one's particular concern

definitions.meaning: a homing bird, sometimes called a homer, used for racing
in the British idiom 'that's not my ...', the word means one's own business or responsibility

explanation.walkthrough: Homer looks like the Greek poet; it is a homing bird. 'That's not my pigeon' is an old British idiom for 'not my business'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a racing homer bird and, in an old British idiom, one's own business.

clue.text: Old pig food found around this vessel

indicators.note: one piece found around another surrounds it

parts.note: slops are waste food fed to pigs

explanation.surface: Ancient pigswill turned up near the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing boat, a vessel.

clue.text: Drink creamy brew in most potent state

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and concoct, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sipping a rich frothy brew is the ultimate state to be in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' looks like part of the drink, a creamy brew, but it is the signal to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremacy is the condition of being highest in power or authority over others.

clue.text: Aging eccentric seen with bouquet

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the bouquet of a wine is its scent

explanation.surface: An oddball old person is spotted carrying a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns SEEN into SENE; bouquet is the smell of wine, not flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent means growing old, the biological process of deterioration with age.

clue.text: Illness of moping owl on ivy-mantled tower?

definitions.text: of moping owl on ivy-mantled tower?
definitions.meaning: Gray's Elegy says the moping owl from the ivy-mantled tower does to the moon complain, so this is the owl's grievance

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition quotes Thomas Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard', where the owl laments from the tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or ailment, and also a grievance voiced, as by Gray's owl.

clue.text: Accommodating type, Jersey's saint, carrying holy books

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside

parts.note: St Helier is the patron saint of Jersey and the name of its capital
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Hebrew Bible

explanation.surface: A kindly person from Jersey, a saint, carries some scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodating' looks like 'obliging'; literally, an hotelier provides accommodation. Jersey is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel, providing lodging for guests.

clue.text: Participate in bingo in place of entertainment

parts.note: to play is to take part in a game
house is an old name for the game bingo, called housey-housey

explanation.surface: Joining in a game of bingo at a leisure venue.
explanation.walkthrough: House is an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a theatre, a venue where people go for entertainment.

clue.text: Public sale that's halted by passing trio

definitions.meaning: a sale where goods go to the highest bidder
in bridge, the bidding ends once three players in a row say no bid

explanation.walkthrough: 'passing trio' is a bridge term: the bidding round, also named with this word, ends after three consecutive passes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sale by competitive bidding and the bidding phase in bridge.

clue.text: Double figure

definitions.meaning: a spitting likeness of someone, as in 'the very ... of his father'
a picture or representation of a form

explanation.definitionFit: An image is both a close likeness of someone and a pictured representation.

clue.text: Strong wind trapping 50 aboard sailing-ship

indicators.note: something trapping another holds it inside

parts.note: a gale is a very strong wind
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to be on a ship is to be aboard

explanation.surface: A storm traps fifty people on board an old sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked ship powered by sail, used from the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Riddle about knight confused 19

indicators.note: one piece placed about another surrounds it
something confused is mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, meaning double or figure
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A puzzling knight is muddled about a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the 19-across answer into EIGMA, and 'about' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or puzzle, something hard to understand.

clue.text: Former copper's drug plea

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the possessive adds S
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman pleads about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse is a reason offered in defence, a plea to justify oneself.

clue.text: No opera house at first in this state capital

indicators.note: something placed at first goes to the front of the rest

parts.note: taken as written
Lulu is an opera by Alban Berg

explanation.surface: The capital has no opera house, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' looks like it picks a first letter, but it sends HO to the front of NO + LULU. The city is the capital of Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city of the US state of Hawaii.

clue.text: His charges are small, but have a sting in the tail

definitions.text: His charges are small, but have a sting in the tail

parts.words: His charges are small, but have a sting in the tail
parts.note: the charges are not fees but the creatures in someone's care, tiny insects with stings at their rear ends

explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' reads as prices; they are the bees a keeper looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist is a beekeeper, and bees are small insects with stings.

clue.text: British coin once recognised in an African republic

definitions.meaning: an old gold coin worth 21 shillings
a West African country whose capital is Conakry

explanation.walkthrough: The old British gold coin, worth 21 shillings, took its name from the African region where its gold came from.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an obsolete British coin of 21 shillings and a West African state.

clue.text: Over there it's done, roughly, in a year

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: YR is the abbreviation for year

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A job over there got sloppily finished within a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for that place in the distance, at a distance from here.

clue.text: Making great demands unknown in English theatre work

parts.note: in algebra x stands for an unknown quantity
acting is the work of a performer on stage

explanation.surface: Stage work in England is hugely taxing for an unknown actor.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra X is the conventional unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding a great deal of effort or precision, as an exacting task.
